title: Traditional Festival March 3
simplified_paragraphs: 农历三月初三是中国多个民族共同的传统节日， 最早起源于古代汉族的上巳节。 古人认为三月的第一个巳日适合去水边洗澡， 用清水洗去坏运气。 后来这个节日被固定在三月三， 内容逐渐从祈福发展为春游、 宴饮等轻松活动。 人们会在水边喝酒作诗， 青年男女也借此机会唱歌约会， 形成了独特的节日文化。

随着时间推移， 汉族地区的三月三慢慢变得冷清， 但在南方少数民族中却焕发了新生命。 壮族人民把这一天变成盛大的歌会， 成千上万人聚集对歌。 未婚青年用抛绣球、 碰彩蛋的方式表达心意， 家家户户还会制作象征吉祥的五色糯米饭。 侗族的庆祝活动充满竞技趣味， 青年们争抢空中落下的彩环， 姑娘们用精心准备的菜篮传递情意， 寨子里回荡着芦笙舞的欢快节奏。 布依族人带着敬畏祭祀山神， 青年们边撒玉米粒防虫害边唱情歌。 畲族人吃着黑色糯米饭纪念古代英雄， 夜晚围着篝火跳起传统舞蹈。 黎族男女穿戴彩色饰品对歌定情， 用竹筒饭和米酒表达对祖先的怀念。 瑶族男子提前进山打猎， 妇女们染制彩色糯米饭准备家宴。 苗族青年通过射花比赛选择伴侣， 有些地方还举办热闹的摔跤大会。 仡佬族人集体到祖坟前跳舞祭祀， 也为新生命举办特别的仪式。 高山族通过夜渔祭祈求丰收。 不同民族为这个节日注入了独特内涵。
这个节日既保留着古老传统， 又充满生活气息。 虽然各地习俗不同， 但都包含着对自然的敬畏、 对丰收的期盼， 以及青年男女追求幸福的美好愿望。 五色糯米饭、 彩色鸡蛋、 山歌对唱等共同元素， 见证着各民族文化的交流与融合。 从水边祈福到春日欢庆， 三月三就像一条多彩的丝带， 将中国不同民族的传统智慧和生活热情紧紧联系在一起。

這個節日既保留著古老傳統， 又充滿生活氣息。 雖然各地習俗不同， 但都包含著對自然的敬畏、 對豐收的期盼， 以及青年男女追求幸福的美好願望。 五色糯米飯、 彩色雞蛋、 山歌對唱等共同元素， 見證著各民族文化的交流與融合。 從水邊祈福到春日歡慶， 三月三就像一條多彩的絲帶， 將中國不同民族的傳統智慧和生活熱情緊緊聯繫在一起。
pinyin_paragraphs: nóng lì Sān yuè chū sān shì Zhōng guó duō gè mín zú gòng tóng de chuán tǒng jié rì，  zuì zǎo qǐ yuán yú gǔ dài Hàn zú de Shàng sì jié。  gǔ rén rèn wéi Sān yuè de dì yī gè sì rì shì hé qù shuǐ biān xǐ zǎo，  yòng qīng shuǐ xǐ qù huài yùn qi。  hòu lái zhè gè jié rì bèi gù dìng zài Sān yuè sān，  nèi róng zhú jiàn cóng qí fú fā zhǎn wéi chūn yóu、  yàn yǐn děng qīng sōng huó dòng。  rén men huì zài shuǐ biān hē jiǔ zuò shī，  qīng nián nán nǚ yě jiè cǐ jī huì chàng gē yuē huì，  xíng chéng le dú tè de jié rì wén huà。

suí zhe shí jiān tuī yí，  Hàn zú dì qū de Sān yuè sān màn màn biàn de lěng qīng，  dàn zài nán fāng shǎo shù mín zú zhōng què huàn fā le xīn shēng mìng。  Zhuàng zú rén mín bǎ zhè yī tiān biàn chéng shèng dà de gē huì，  chéng qiān shàng wàn rén jù jí duì gē。  wèi hūn qīng nián yòng pāo xiù qiú、  pèng cǎi dàn de fāng shì biǎo dá xīn yì，  jiā jiā hù hù hái huì zhì zuò xiàng zhēng jí xiáng de wǔ sè nuò mǐ fàn。  Dòng zú de qìng zhù huó dòng chōng mǎn jìng jì qù wèi，  qīng nián men zhēng qiǎng kōng zhōng luò xià de cǎi huán，  gū niang men yòng jīng xīn zhǔn bèi de cài lán chuán dì qíng yì，  zhàizi lǐ huí dàng zhe lú shēng wǔ de huān kuài jié zòu。  Bù yī zú rén dài zhe jìng wèi jì sì shān shén，  qīng nián men biān sǎ yù mǐ lì fáng chóng hài biān chàng qíng gē。  Shē zú rén chī zhe hēi sè nuò mǐ fàn jì niàn gǔ dài yīng xióng，  yè wǎn wéi zhe gōu huǒ tiào qǐ chuán tǒng wǔ dǎo。  Lí zú nán nǚ chuān dài cǎi sè shì pǐn duì gē dìng qíng，  yòng zhú tǒng fàn hé mǐ jiǔ biǎo dá duì zǔ xiān de huái niàn。  Yáo zú nán zǐ tí qián jìn shān dǎ liè，  fù nǚ men rǎn zhì cǎi sè nuò mǐ fàn zhǔn bèi jiā yàn。  Miáo zú qīng nián tōng guò shè huā bǐ sài xuǎn zé bàn lǚ，  yǒu xiē dì fang hái jǔ bàn rè nao de shuāi jiāo dà huì。  Gē lǎo zú rén jí tǐ dào zǔ fén qián tiào wǔ jì sì，  yě wèi xīn shēng mìng jǔ bàn tè bié de yí shì。  Gāo shān zú tōng guò yè yú jì qí qiú fēng shōu。  bù tóng mín zú wèi zhè gè jié rì zhù rù le dú tè nèi hán。

zhè gè jié rì jì bǎo liú zhe gǔ lǎo chuán tǒng，  yòu chōng mǎn shēng huó qì xī。  suī rán gè dì xí sú bù tóng，  dàn dōu bāo hán zhe duì zì rán de jìng wèi、  duì fēng shōu de qī pàn，  yǐ jí qīng nián nán nǚ zhuī qiú xìng fú de měi hǎo yuàn wàng。  wǔ sè nuò mǐ fàn、  cǎi sè jī dàn、  shān gē duì chàng děng gòng tóng yuán sù，  jiàn zhèng zhe gè mín zú wén huà de jiāo liú yǔ róng hé。  cóng shuǐ biān qí fú dào chūn rì huān qìng，  Sān yuè sān jiù xiàng yī tiáo duō cǎi de sī dài，  jiāng Zhōng guó bù tóng mín zú de chuán tǒng zhì huì hé shēng huó rè qíng jǐn jǐn lián xì zài yī qǐ。
english_paragraphs: The third day of the third lunar month is a traditional festival shared by many ethnic groups in China. It originated from the Shangsi Festival of the ancient Han people. The ancients believed that the first day of March was a good time to take a bath by the water and wash away bad luck with clean water. Later, this festival was fixed on March 3rd, and its content gradually developed from praying for blessings to spring outings, banquets and other relaxed activities. People would drink and compose poems by the water, and young men and women would also take this opportunity to sing and date, forming a unique festival culture.

As time goes by, March 3rd gradually becomes deserted in Han areas, but it takes on new life among ethnic minorities in the south. The Zhuang people turn this day into a grand singing party, with thousands of people gathering to sing antiphonal songs. Unmarried young people express their feelings by throwing hydrangeas and touching colored eggs. Every household also makes five-color glutinous rice, which symbolizes good luck. The celebrations of the Dong people are full of competitive fun. Young people compete for colorful rings falling from the sky. Girls convey their affection with carefully prepared vegetable baskets. The cheerful rhythm of Lusheng dance echoes in the village. Buyi people worship the mountain gods with reverence, and young people sing love songs while scattering corn kernels to prevent pests. The She people eat black glutinous rice to commemorate ancient heroes and perform traditional dances around the bonfire at night. Li men and women wear colorful ornaments, sing songs to express their love, and use bamboo tube rice and rice wine to express their nostalgia for their ancestors. The Yao men go into the mountains to hunt in advance, and the women dye colorful glutinous rice to prepare for the family banquet. Miao youths choose their partners through flower-shooting competitions, and lively wrestling conferences are also held in some places. The Gelao people collectively go to their ancestral graves to dance and offer sacrifices, and also hold special ceremonies for new life. The Gaoshan people pray for a good harvest through the night fishing festival. Different ethnic groups inject unique connotations into this festival.

This festival not only retains ancient traditions but is also full of life. Although customs vary from place to place, they all contain the reverence for nature, the expectation for a good harvest, and the good wishes of young men and women to pursue happiness. Common elements such as five-color glutinous rice, colorful eggs, and folk song duets bear witness to the exchange and integration of cultures of various ethnic groups. From praying by the waterside to celebrating spring, March 3rd is like a colorful ribbon that closely connects the traditional wisdom and enthusiasm for life of different ethnic groups in China.
